response_text: The distinction between the “user” and the “kernel” in our OS project is reflected in how code is organized into main.c and kernel.c. Code in main.c represents the user-level program, which is what the user wants to run, like creating and running threads or printing output. In contrast, kernel.c contains the operating system code that manages low-level tasks such as context switching, scheduling, and stack management. This separation is important because it allows the user to write programs without worrying about the complex inner workings of the OS. It also keeps the system modular and safer, as bugs in user code don’t directly affect kernel behavior, and the kernel can enforce boundaries to prevent misuse of system resources.\n
